first.rationale: The immediate competitive threat is explicitly concentrated in price-sensitive SMB accounts, where targeted promotional pricing previously produced strong acquisition and revenue lift. Verify the pricing result and compare its durability against onboarding evidence before committing; use a guarded, segment-specific test to protect long-term value and avoid broad discounting.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and showed higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than discounted acquisition. Promotional pricing is ruled out for this cycle because its verified retention decline (-12%) conflicts with the long-term objective.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than pivot to promotional pricing. The only verified pricing evidence shows a 12% 30-day retention decline, and a deeper competitor cut makes a discount escalation especially likely to attract low-durability revenue. Simplified onboarding directly addresses the observed completion decline and has verified improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. The immediate SMB churn signal is material, so monitor it as a downstream risk, but do not trade sustainable revenue for an unverified discount response.
